cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a woven palm-fibre sombrero with leather appliqué (horseshoe motif) and black-and-white banding — a type of hat traditionally produced in the palm-weaving regions of northeastern Mexico, including areas inhabited by the Huastec; palm hat-making is a recognized craft of this region.

physical.title: hat
physical.summary: Hat; made of braided palm fibre, coiled and sewn together; tall crown, top concave, with raised bar from front to back; wide brim slightly curled, edge folded over a piece of string, which is tied at back and left as tassel; strip of black leather folded over brim and sewn in place, square holes cut in leather exposing white plastic underneath, creating alternating black and white squares around brim; black leather hatband with white scalloped trim on top sewn around base of crown, sections of black leather cut out to reveal white leather underneath, at front and back section cut out in shape of horseshoe, with sections of white leather also cut out to reveal black plastic underneath, in alternating squares; on each side near top, white leather with black leather horseshoe sewn on top, sections of black leather horseshoe cut out to reveal white plastic underneath in alternating squares; at centre of horseshoe two black metal rivets with leather thong threaded through to tie hat to head.
